auditor: Research Alliance for New York City Schools
title: Building Teacher Capacity for Equitable CS: Insights from NYC’s CS4All Initiative
plain_title: What happened after city teachers were trained to teach coding
what_they_audited: A research report from the Research Alliance for New York City Schools, a research center at New York University that studies the city's public schools, on how the Computer Science for All initiative prepared teachers and how many of them went on to teach computer science. It examines who took part in training, who stayed, who implemented and what got in the way.
background: Computer Science for All, known as CS4All, is a public-private partnership launched by New York City Public Schools in 2015 to bring computer science to every student in each grade band. It depended on providing professional learning to large numbers of teachers and school leaders, many with little or no computer science background, along with training in culturally relevant and sustaining education practices.

recommendations: Keep providing ongoing professional learning, curriculum resources and communities of practice for computer science teachers, and consider which supports can be delivered virtually or asynchronously to reach more teachers at lower cost.
Continue embedding culturally responsive-sustaining education practices in computer science training as a way to improve instruction and students' sense of belonging in the subject.
Give school leaders support and resources to plan for computer science, since administrators set the vision, protect instructional time and manage competing demands.
Address the structural barriers directly, with systemic solutions to staffing shortages, scheduling constraints and how resources are allocated.
Align the initiative with district-wide priorities by making sure superintendents and executive superintendents understand computer science education and can back up school leaders with resources.

Build long-term capacity through teacher preparation tied to classroom-tested curriculum, certification pathways, incentives and school supports, so the city can prepare and keep qualified computer science teachers.
